Title: Shift-Robust Quality Prediction in Sugar Crystallization Using Physics-Guided Gradient Boosting
Affiliations: Department of Computer Science, College of Engineering and Computer Science, Jazan University, Jazan, Saudi Arabia
Authors with affiliations: Martin R.J., Department of Computer Science, College of Engineering and Computer Science, Jazan University, Jazan, Saudi Arabia; Khawaji A., Department of Computer Science, College of Engineering and Computer Science, Jazan University, Jazan, Saudi Arabia
Abstract: Sugar crystallization is a tightly controlled unit operation in which variations in supersaturation, temperature, and impurity load can directly affect Brix, purity, color, and crystal size. However, data-driven soft sensors often face limited labeled data, measurement noise, missing observations, and poor generalization under changing operating conditions. This study presents a synthetic digital-twin benchmark for vacuum pan crystallization and a physics-guided machine-learning framework based on gradient-boosting decision trees for simultaneous prediction of multiple quality attributes. The benchmark generates batch trajectories using simplified mass–energy balances and crystallization-rate proxies, while incorporating industrially relevant sensor noise, drift, missingness, actuator lag, feed-quality disturbances, and operating-regime shifts. Windowed process histories are transformed into process-informed descriptors and used to train gradient-boosting models for Brix, purity, color, and crystal-size prediction. Physical plausibility was assessed through process-informed features, monotonicity checks, and residual-based scoring, while robustness was evaluated using in-distribution (Test-ID) and out-of-distribution (Test-OOD) scenarios and conformal prediction intervals. The proposed models achieved strong nominal performance for Brix, purity, and crystal size, with Test-ID RMSE values of 0.440, 0.810, and 18.502, respectively. Under operating shifts, Brix and purity remained comparatively stable, whereas color and crystal size showed greater performance degradation, indicating higher sensitivity to regime changes. Conformal analysis provided informative uncertainty estimates under nominal conditions but revealed reduced coverage under Test-OOD conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of gradient-boosting soft sensors for crystallization monitoring while highlighting the need for improved uncertainty quantification and distribution-shift resilience for reliable industrial deployment. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Society for Sugar Research & Promotion 2026.

Abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional methods of dam displacement prediction are difficult to handle long-term time series, this paper proposes an interval intelligent prediction model that integrates the Golden Damped Sine Cosine Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (GDPSO), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), self-attention mechanism, and Quantile Regression (QR). By incorporating the selfattention mechanism to enhance LSTM's ability for capturing global dependencies, and utilizing GDPSO for hyperparameter optimization, a high-precision point prediction model (GDPSO-LSTM-attention) is developed. Further combining QR to quantify model uncertainty, the model achieved interval prediction of displacement. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms comparative models in both accuracy and trend tracking, and effectively quantifies prediction uncertainty, which provides foundational support for the "Four Preventions" construction of digital twin platforms in smart water conservancy. © 2026 Huazhong University of Science and Technology. Abstract: The health of the ecosystem, quality of human life, and sustainable development of society and economy are directly related to the quality and safety of the water environment in a watershed. Digital twin technology offers new possibilities for simulating and applying water environment models. This study constructed hydrodynamic and pollutant migration models for a three-dimensional reservoir and a one-dimensional river in Danjiangkou Basin. Aiming at the uncertainty of sudden water pollution incidents in basin, the scenario simulation technology for pollution incidents occurring at any location had been developed, achieving the rapid construction of sudden water pollution scenarios and the simulation of the effects of emergency response measures. This study offers technical support for the intelligent management of the water environment in the digital twin Danjiangkou, which provides reference and experience for water environment management in other basins. © 2025 Huazhong University of Science and Technology. Abstract: ［Objective］ In response to the pressing need for intelligent transformation in equipment support for China Coast Guard vessels, this paper presents a systematic review of research progress in ship fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) systems based on large language models (LLMs). Shipboard environments pose unique challenges, including weak communication links at sea, limited onboard computational resources, high levels of mechanical noise, and stringent reliability requirements for safety-critical systems. Traditional datadriven FDD methods, while leveraging accumulated industrial IoT data, suffer from a scarcity of high-quality labeled data and limited cross-scenario generalization capability. LLMs offer new opportunities due to their capabilities in multi-modal understanding, knowledge fusion, and zero-shot or few-shot reasoning. ［Method］A systematic literature review methodology was adopted to analyze 95 relevant publications from 2022 to 2026. The search was conducted across Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and CNKI databases using keyword combinations including "fault diagnosis", "fault detection", "large language model", "LLM", "GPT", "PHM", "intelligent operation and maintenance", and "agent". After initial screening of titles and abstracts, followed by backward snowballing, 95 papers were ultimately included for analysis. LLM opti mization strategies in industrial FDD were summarized into four dimensions: input-side enhancement (including RAG, knowledge graphs, multi-modal LLMs, and digital twins), model-side optimization (including finetuning or retraining, prompt engineering, and multi-model collaboration), output-side refinement (feedback optimization), and architectural design (integrating LLMs with signal processing, machine learning, neural networks, and multi-agent systems). In response to the characteristics of shipboard data heterogeneity, limited computational resources, and stringent reliability requirements, a hierarchical, decoupled, multi-agent collaborative reference architecture for shipboard FDD systems is proposed. The architecture consists of five layers from top to bottom: the interaction layer (supporting multi-modal input and adaptive output), the agent layer (comprising eight specialized agents for reception, scheduling, query, process management, reasoning, generation, data processing, and feedback), the model layer (including a domain-specific fine-tuned LLM, an embedding model, and a lightweight multi-modal model), the tool layer (featuring time-series signal processing with dual pipelines for feature extraction and semantic mapping, along with text processing, vector embedding, multi-modal alignment, and knowledge graph tools), and the data layer (containing a raw database, a vector knowledge base, and a knowledge graph).［Results］The number of research publications on LLMs in the industrial FDD field increased from 4 in 2023 to 22 in 2024, and further surged to 61 in 2025, with approximately 76% focusing on input-side enhancement and model-side optimization. This trend indicates rapidly growing research interest and the significant potential of LLMs in this domain. For shipboard scenarios, the proposed architecture supports localized deployment of lightweight LLMs through quantization and pruning techniques, enabling multi-source data fusion via vector knowledge bases and knowledge graphs. Based on multi-agent collaboration, it enables automatic task decomposition for fault diagnosis and closed-loop decision-making. The architecture also incorporates mechanisms for uncertainty-aware conflict resolution (including historical accuracy-based confidence calibration, external hard-constraint anchoring, and conservative decision strategies), multi-agent overhead optimization (on-demand activation, hierarchical context management, agent role consolidation, and asynchronous task scheduling), and adaptation to unknown faults (zero-shot reasoning with LLM prior knowledge, cross-device fault pattern transfer, active learning with human-in-the-loop annotation, and synthetic data augmentation).［Conclusion］The proposed hierarchical reference architecture provides a feasible pathway and framework for transforming shipboard FDD systems toward an intelligent paradigm driven by the synergy of data and knowledge. Future research should focus on trustworthy outputs, adaptive capabilities, and system integration to enhance equipment support efficiency and navigation safety. Key future directions include robust intelligence under strong constraints (multi-modal signal characterization under highnoise conditions, and LLM decision trustworthiness assessment compliant with IEC 61508 functional safety requirements), continuous self-adaptation in offline environments (ontological incremental learning and knowledge distillation during communication blackouts, and few-shot or zero-shot cross-device fault transfer diagnosis), and system integration with standardization (standardized interfaces with existing ship cyberphysical systems, and verification and validation methods compliant with China Classification Society specifications). © 2026, Editorial Department of Chinese Journal of Ship Research. Title: Wildfire digital twins: a paradigm shift from monitoring systems to intelligent decision infrastructures

Abstract: Wildfires are becoming more frequent, severe, and complex driven by global warming and climate change, posing escalating threats to ecosystems, infrastructure, public health, and community safety worldwide. Recent advances in Earth observation, artificial intelligence, physics-based modelling, and cyberinfrastructure have accelerated the development of wildfire digital twins (WFDTs), yet existing capabilities remain fragmented across monitoring, fusion, prediction, simulation, and decision support. Unlike prior reviews that primarily address individual aspect of wildfire, this review and vision paper provides an integrated synthesis of WFDTs. We propose a six-layer WFDT architecture, identify six core capabilities spanning situational awareness through adaptive learning, and organise applications across the wildfire lifecycle from prevention and detection to response, smoke management, and post-fire recovery. Building upon these advances, we outline a research roadmap toward autonomous WFDTs through advances in hybrid intelligence, trustworthy AI, uncertainty quantification, decision intelligence, and continual learning. We envision that the defining characteristic of future WFDTs is not increasingly realistic digital representation, but their evolution into a new paradigm that continuously integrates sensing, prediction, uncertainty quantification, optimisation, governance, and human expertise towards a paradigm of intelligent, trustworthy decision infrastructures that continuously support human-centred wildfire decision making. © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: Addressing the challenges of dynamic uncertainty, heterogeneity of multi-source information, and excessive cognitive load on decision-makers in modern warehousing and logistics systems, traditional fuzzy decision-making methods (e.g., traditional fuzzy analytic hierarchy process) struggle to achieve real-Time adaptive optimization. This study proposes a hybrid intelligent decision-making model based on human-machine collaboration, termed HMIDM. The model first employs dynamic intuitionistic fuzzy sets to handle time-varying uncertainty in the warehousing environment. Second, it introduces an improved D-S evidence theory to fuse multi-source IoT data with expert fuzzy preferences. Finally, a dynamic responsibility transfer mechanism between human and machine is constructed, which automatically switches between manual intervention and algorithmic autonomous decision-making according to decision confidence. Through simulation validation in an automated stereoscopic warehouse, the model achieves a 12.7% improvement in decision accuracy in scenarios of storage location assignment and retrieval path selection, while significantly reducing manual decision delays under abnormal operating conditions. This study provides a new theoretical paradigm for intelligent decision-making in digital twin warehousing systems. © (2026) by Aussino Academic Publishing House All rights reserved.

Abstract: Smart polymer composite actuators are emerging as enabling materials for next-generation soft robotics by combining mechanical compliance, multifunctionality, and programmable responsiveness within lightweight architectures. Their ability to convert electrical, thermal, magnetic, optical, and chemical stimuli into controlled deformation provides advantages for adaptive interaction with complex environments. Advances in three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) printing have expanded their design space through multimaterial integration, spatially programmed architectures, functional gradients, and time-dependent shape transformation. Concurrently, machine learning (ML) offers new opportunities for material discovery, structure–property prediction, fabrication optimization, actuator modeling, inverse design, sensing, and intelligent control. This review critically examines the integration of polymer composites, 3D/4D printing, computational modeling, and ML across the materials-to-device development chain, from formulation and architecture to manufacturing, actuation, sensing, control, and lifecycle monitoring. Particular attention is given to printability–functionality trade-offs, multimaterial interfaces, manufacturing scalability and reproducibility, dataset limitations, uncertainty, simulation-to-reality transfer, and model generalization. Emerging strategies, including physics-informed ML, multiscale density functional theory–molecular dynamics–ML frameworks, digital twins, closed-loop design–print–test optimization, and sustainable composite systems, are discussed as pathways toward more predictive and efficient development. The review emphasizes that high ML accuracy does not necessarily ensure transferability or reliable physical performance and highlights the need for standardized validation and experimentally grounded models. Finally, opportunities for increasingly autonomous, self-adaptive, and closed-loop soft robotic systems are outlined, providing a roadmap toward reliable, scalable, sustainable, and application-ready intelligent soft robotic technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects

Abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) has become an important public-health tool for tracking community-level circulation of emerging and re-emerging pathogens, but wastewater measurements are not directly interpretable public-health indicators. Signals recovered from sewer systems are shaped by sampling variability, environmental and inter- and intra-laboratory variations, population-dependent bias, and high-dimensional molecular complexity. Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used to extract predictive and decision-relevant information from these data, but the strength of the supporting evidence varies substantially. This narrative review examines how strongly current applications are supported by published evidence. Sources were identified through iterative searches of three literature-search sources updated to June 2026 and classified by role, analytical task, and strength of evidence. To keep the analytical scope consistent, we use a pragmatic four-layer classification: classical statistical models, conventional machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid or mechanistically informed approaches. Applications are reviewed across five analytical tasks: predictive modelling and forecasting, anomaly and fluctuation detection, data harmonization and normalization, high-dimensional interpretation, and integrated decision support. Among 35 sources reporting analytical or modelling work, 25 analyzed SARS-CoV-2 alone; demonstrated early-warning evidence came predominantly from L1 methods, and most target–task combinations remain prospective. Even within SARS-CoV-2 surveillance, reported performance was context-dependent. We examine the data-quality, methodological, and implementation barriers that limit broader application and validation. Future priorities include standardized and collaborative frameworks, multimodal data fusion, mechanistic and digital-twin modelling with explicit uncertainty assessment, and transparent and actionable analytics, with broader surveillance applications constrained by governance and public acceptability. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Digital and Computational Methods for Sustainable Urban Transitions: A Critical Narrative Review Through Urban Design
Affiliations: Department of Architecture, University of Cyprus, Nicosia, 1678, Cyprus
Authors with affiliations: Savvides A.L., Department of Architecture, University of Cyprus, Nicosia, 1678, Cyprus
Abstract: The accelerating convergence of urbanization, climate change, and digital transformation is reshaping how cities are conceived, designed, and managed. This critical narrative review asks one central question: how can newly emerging digital capabilities and established computational and decision-support methods, when applied in novel or rapidly evolving ways, support accountable urban-design decisions for sustainable urban transitions? “Emerging” is used here selectively for capabilities characterized by recent technical development, rapid diffusion, limited implementation maturity, or new urban-design applications—not as a label for established methods such as GIS, BIM, AHP/ANP, or parametric modelling. The review is organized by functional stage in the urban-design process: (i) conceptual and technological foundations; (ii) urban analysis and systems interpretation; (iii) computational design support; (iv) decision-making and spatial intervention; and (v) outcome evaluation and feedback. Across these stages, comparative evidence is used to examine function, data requirements, spatial scale, application stage, empirical maturity, risks, and limitations. The synthesis indicates that digital and computational methods are most useful when they augment rather than displace professional and civic judgement, make trade-offs and uncertainty explicit, and connect evidence to context-sensitive spatial intervention. Urban design is therefore treated not as the sole driver of transition but as a mediating spatial practice within wider planning, governance, socio-technical, and socio-ecological processes. © 2026 by the author.

Title: Identifying root causes and propagation paths of systemic cybersecurity risks in digital twins: a mixed-method approach
Affiliations: Baskent University, Ankara, Turkey; Bartin University, Bartin, Turkey; Ankara Yildirim Beyazit University, Ankara, Turkey; Republic of Turkey Ministry of Industry and Technology, Ankara, Turkey
Authors with affiliations: Erol İ., Baskent University, Ankara, Turkey; Oztel A., Bartin University, Bartin, Turkey; Medeni I.T., Ankara Yildirim Beyazit University, Ankara, Turkey; Ar İ.M., Republic of Turkey Ministry of Industry and Technology, Ankara, Turkey
Abstract: Purpose – This study addresses the research gap in understanding systemic interdependencies among cybersecurity challenges in digital twins (DTs) by proposing a novel framework to model these relationships under uncertainty, supporting anticipatory governance in critical sectors such as healthcare. Design/methodology/approach – A mixed methods approach combines a systematic literature review with a Picture Fuzzy Interpretive Structural Modeling and MICMAC (PF-ISM MICMAC) framework. Picture fuzzy sets capture indeterminacy and refusal in expert judgments from a multidisciplinary panel of experts. Robustness is validated through 10, 000 Monte Carlo simulations and a leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, complemented by semi-structured interviews. Findings – Ten key cybersecurity challenges are identified. Lack of standardization and regulation, infrastructure vulnerabilities and inadequate resilience metrics emerge as foundational drivers. Data poisoning, secure communication and lack of interoperability are linkage factors with high driving and dependence power, forming a dynamic risk core. Insider threats and lack of system resilience are dependent outcomes. Validation confirms high structural stability and practical relevance. Practical implications – Policy: Urges global regulatory harmonization and standardized security frameworks for DTs. Managerial: Provides a risk-based prioritization heuristic that invests in high driving factors, integrates responses for linkage factors and monitors dependent outcomes. Originality/value – This study does not claim to invent a wholly new methodology. Rather, its originality lies in: (1) the novel application of the PF-ISM MICMAC framework to model systemic interdependencies among DT cybersecurity challenges, a domain where prior research has treated challenges as independent and (2) the empirically grounded and validated six-level hierarchical framework, which enables proactive systemic risk analysis. © Emerald Publishing Limited

Abstract: Dynamic inductive charging (DIC) combined with hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities offers a promising pathway toward extended-range electric vehicles with grid integration benefits. However, real-time optimal energy management remains challenging due to multi-axis coil misalignment, component aging, and bidirectional power flow uncertainty. This paper proposes an adaptive digital twin driven artificial intelligence (AI) energy management framework integrating physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), soft actor critic (SAC) deep reinforcement learning, and model predictive control (MPC) for optimal power distribution among a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC), lithium-ion battery, supercapacitor, dynamic wireless charging, and grid interface in four-wheel drive electric vehicles (4WD-EVs). The framework features: (1) a self-evolving digital twin with online learning via Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) updating every 50 cycles; (2) a PINN-based state estimator for battery-state estimation, with an average inference time of 1.1 ms and a worst-case latency of 2.8 ms; (3) a hierarchical SAC–MPC strategy with high-level mode selection and low-level power optimization; (4) real-time five-degree-of-freedom WPT misalignment compensation, achieving a mean efficiency of 91.5% under the evaluated dynamic lateral misalignment conditions, with a 50 mm displacement amplitude; (5) degradation-aware V2G optimization generating €582.50/year in revenue while reducing battery aging by 31.8%; and (6) comprehensive techno-economic analysis yielding a discounted payback period of approximately 5.57 years and a net present value of approximately €3777 over a 10-year horizon. Validated through 200+ hours of hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation on the dSPACE/NVIDIA Jetson platform, the proposed approach achieves a 24.3% cost reduction and 31.8% lower battery degradation. The MPC controller exhibits an average execution time of 32.1 ms, a 95th-percentile latency of 44.8 ms, and a worst-case latency of 62.4 ms, while remaining within the 100-ms real-time control deadline. Results demonstrate the viability of adaptive digital twins for next-generation EVs with autonomous charging and multi-source architectures. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: System identification of high-speed planing hulls with Bayesian Hankel extended dynamic mode decomposition with control
Affiliations: National Research Council-Institute of Marine Engineering, CNR-INM, Rome, Italy; The University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA, United States
Authors with affiliations: Palma G., National Research Council-Institute of Marine Engineering, CNR-INM, Rome, Italy; Serani A., National Research Council-Institute of Marine Engineering, CNR-INM, Rome, Italy; Stern F., The University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA, United States; Diez M., National Research Council-Institute of Marine Engineering, CNR-INM, Rome, Italy
Abstract: A data-driven, equation-free framework based on Bayesian Hankel extended dynamic mode decomposition with control (BHeDMDc) is presented to forecast the dynamic behavior of a generic prismatic planing hull (GPPH). Specifically, the investigation focuses on towed vessel operations within irregular head wave environments. By isolating spatiotemporal coherent modes from intricate vessel dynamics, the proposed methodology enhances robustness against transient and nonlinear phenomena through time-delay embeddings and extended observables. Furthermore, the integration of control inputs improves forecasting accuracy, while a Bayesian framework provides robust probabilistic uncertainty quantification. The capability of BHeDMDc is evaluated through the reconstruction of both hydrodynamic forces and motion variables. Results demonstrate that the algorithm successfully captures primary dynamic traits in real time, making it highly suitable for digital twin frameworks. Crucially, the approach resolves two distinct tasks: the direct problem of forecasting seakeeping motions from wave inputs, and the inverse problem of estimating forces acting on the hull using easily accessible onboard motion measurements. Ultimately, this work underscores the viability of uncertainty-aware, data-driven models for high-speed craft, laying the groundwork for future advancements involving experimental validation and real-time adaptive capabilities. © China Ship Scientific Research Center 2026.

Title: Dynamic decarbonization pathways for inland shipping under energy system and policy uncertainties

Abstract: Inland shipping decarbonization requires coordinated changes in fleets, fuels, infrastructure, and policy that static life cycle assessments cannot capture. This study develops a framework coupling Power-to-X pathways, dynamic hybrid life cycle assessment, a fleet digital twin, and multi-objective optimization. Applied to 2,100 weighted representative vessel records in the Yangtze River Delta from 2025 to 2050 under four policy scenarios, the selected integrated policy knee solution reduces diesel from 99.0% to 15.5% of fleet shaft energy demand. Battery electricity becomes the largest low-carbon pathway (30.3%), followed by hydrogen (22.1%), e-methanol (16.4%), and ammonia (15.6%). Cumulative life cycle emissions are 298.8 Mt CO2-eq, 10.4% below business as usual, while net present resource cost is 166.3 billion 2025 USD. Deep inland shipping decarbonization is feasible but back-loaded and depends on coordinated fleet renewal, infrastructure deployment, and fuel diversification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Affiliations: Quantum Serbia, Serbia; Serbian AI Association, Serbia

Abstract: How do data become social capital – more than a corporate asset, a measurable public good that improves health, equity, and sustainability? This chapter answers across four arcs. First, it tracks the analytic stack from OLAP and data mining to Big Data, Deep Learning (DL), and causal, privacy-preserving pipelines, marking the shift from hindsight to intervention. Second, it frames Society 5.0 as human-centred by design: explainability, fairness, and documented governance as operating requirements within edge–core architectures which keep people in the loop. Third, it examines substrates which make real-time analytics feasible at acceptable cost: neuromorphic spiking networks at the edge, photonic linear layers for matrix-heavy inference, and quantum-assisted routines where structure and noise budgets permit – judged by energy per decision, latency, and audit trails rather than headline FLOPS. Finally, applications ground the argument: clinical CNNs, legal Natural Language Processing (NLP), federated learning (FL) for data sovereignty, SHAP for recourse, and physics-informed digital twins which enable therapy planning before intervention. Organoid intelligence (OI) is treated with scientific caution – as exploratory, protocol-sensitive co-processing. The result is a pragmatic roadmap: align models with social outcomes, measure uncertainty and energy, document decisions, and preserve agency – so analytics functions as a civic capability in Society 5.0. © 2027 selection and editorial matter, Amarnath Padhi, Sabyasachi Rath, Elena Gurgu, and Dac-Nhuong Le; individual chapters, the contributors.

Title: A review of data quality challenges and governance approaches in agricultural digital twins

Abstract: Digital twin (DT) technology is emerging as a key enabler for data driven decision making in agriculture. The development of high fidelity agricultural DTs is hindered by a central paradox: the data streams that are used to power DT systems are born with quality deficiencies. While the literature has addressed the technology architecture of agricultural DTs and the application opportunities of agricultural DTs, the poor data quality has been treated as a peripheral issue. The review shows that the quality of data is mysteriously uncertain because of intrinsic bottlenecks associated with the physical acquisition and representation of data, social and technical barriers to data integration and management that amplify data quality uncertainties, and the propagation of data quality uncertainties throughout the DT pipeline to undermine the model outputs and provides decision support to users. To address the issues, the review will postulate a multi-layered governance framework and critique emerging technology pathways regarding AI-cleaning and augmenting data, cloud-edge-terminal collaborative architectures for real-time processing of data, trusted traceability using distributed ledger technology, and dynamic model/data fusion. In conclusion, the development of the intelligent and sustainable production of food will be achieved through a pathway that integrates domain knowledge with artificial intelligence. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to The Brazilian Society of Mechanical Sciences and Engineering 2026.

Title: AI-Driven Agent-Based Urban Digital Twins: A Systematic Literature Review
Affiliations: Technical University of Denmark, Dynamical Systems, Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, Kongens Lyngby, 2800, Denmark; Abertay University, Department of Games Technology and Mathematics, Dundee, DD1 1HG, United Kingdom

Abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) and agent-based approaches to support intelligent and autonomous urban systems. However, existing reviews largely examine DTs, AI techniques, or agent-based approaches separately, leaving limited insight into how these dimensions interact and how such systems progress toward higher levels of intelligence and real-world deployment. This systematic literature review (SLR) analyzes 82 primary research studies describing AI-driven agent-based approaches in urban digital twins as a system of systems and found in four major scientific databases, i.e. IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, and ACM Digital Library. The selected studies were systematically examined with respect to digital twin types, AI techniques used, agent type, agent roles, maturity level, application domains, and key challenges. As a result, we categorize digital twins into five types: conceptual DT, descriptive DT, predictive DT, prescriptive DT and autonomous DT, with the most frequent being the predictive DT. Reinforcement learning emerged as the most common AI technique, while the hierarchical agent taxonomy shows that multi-agent systems dominate at the architectural level, and decision-making and acting is the main role of agents, followed by control. We also identified that most studies remain at relatively low Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) and rely predominantly on simulation-based or conceptual validation, revealing a substantial gap between technological advancement and real-world deployment. The analysis further shows that implementation challenges evolve across the DT life-cycle. Moreover, we found that only a limited proportion of studies explicitly address uncertainty, while the majority rely on deterministic or idealized assumptions. Our analysis further revealed that most urban digital twin systems are in the early stages of development, and we identified key research gaps and, based on this, suggested future research directions. Overall, this SLR provides a structured synthesis of AI-driven agent-based urban digital twins and identifies priorities for interoperability, standardized evaluation, real-world validation, and scalable autonomous urban systems.  © 2013 IEEE.

Title: Reinforcement-Learning-Enabled Supervisory Control of a Full-Scale Anaerobic Digestion Facility Using a Calibrated Digital Twin

Abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) is a cornerstone of energy recovery and decarbonization at wastewater resource recovery facilities (WRRFs), yet full-scale digesters are often operated conservatively due to delayed process feedback, nonlinear stability constraints, and limited observability. This study presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL)-enabled supervisory control framework for full-scale AD that integrates a calibrated mechanistic digital twin model (DTM) with offline policy learning and counterfactual uncertainty evaluation. Specifically, the DTM was calibrated to reproduce control-relevant digester behavior. Using 2.7 years of simulated operation, a batch-constrained Q (BCQ)-reinforcement learning policy was trained to maximize biogas production while penalizing instability associated with pH excursions and elevated volatile fatty acids (VFAs)/alkalinity (ALK) ratios. Counterfactual evaluation against historical, greedy, and heuristic controls used 1 year unseen DTM simulation and 1 year of full-scale operational data. The RL policy achieved comparable mean daily biogas production (+0.35%) in simulated testing. Under the 1 year operational data, it achieved plant-equivalent mean production of 9802 m3/day, corresponding to a modest potential cumulative improvement (+2.7%, 93 405 m3/year) subject to substantial uncertainty P(Δ > 0) = 0.524. These results indicate that offline-trained RL, combined with a mechanistic digital twin and counterfactual evaluation, provides a feasible and interpretable framework for developing and assessing supervisory AD control without live-plant experimentation while showing that the resulting benefit must be interpreted under explicit model-plant uncertainty. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Autonomous Robotaxi Docking Using Digital Twin Vision and LiDAR Planning
Source title: 2026 International Conference on Green Technologies and Sustainable Solutions, GTSS 2026
Affiliations: OH, United States; MI, United States; CA, United States

Abstract: Autonomous robotaxi fleets need a reliable way to charge without human help. For this to work, the charging process must be fully automated. Robotic charging is more demanding than ordinary autonomous parking. The vehicle has to align precisely with a fixed charging interface. The system also depends on accurate perception, motion planning, and manipulator reachability. This study presents a digital-twin-based approach for automated charging. The setup uses both camera and LiDAR sensors. These sensors guide a robotic arm as it connects to the vehicle. The framework includes vehicle-motion planning, charging-port detection, and pose estimation that accounts for uncertainty. A digital twin of the charging station provides key information. It includes charger geometry, docking points, safety zones, and regions with higher uncertainty. The vehicle must reach a suitable docking position so the manipulator can operate within limited pose errors. This requirement defines a docking-constrained task. The system is tested in a CARLA simulation environment. The simulation includes dynamic agents and sensor noise. Results show that planning with docking semantics and uncertainty improves first-attempt connection success. It also reduces the need for late-stage replanning when compared with navigation-focused baselines. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A Digital-Twin-Driven Framework for Traffic and Energy Management Leveraging Generative AI

Abstract: With urbanisation, pressures in urban areas and the pressure of climate are increasing, cities may need smart and data-based decision making by implementing intelligent operations and strategic action architectures. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a revolution in smart city management with the potential to generate such data, perform urban analysis and consider policy alternatives, among other things, when there is an uncertainty. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are the latest generation of urban analytics such as models for generating scenarios and understanding semantic analysis, with diffusion models and large language models (LLMs). Generative models should not be part of decisions, but instead can be used as one end with UDTs and optimization pipeline and integrated within our city decision-support (CDA) architecture. We propose that the next generation is a general model for such a unified model, based on both the global and a customized algorithm based across cities that combines spatio-temporal and digital twin problem modelling methods and models together and provide multivariable approach in urban decision-making from multiple dimensions. We model the framework in traffic signal control and energy demand response tasks on calibrated synthetic cities' urban data. The spatio-temporal GAN (ST-GAN) and conditional VAE (cVAE) are trained and compared to standard deterministic LSTM and Gaussian process baselines based on both the prediction and quality metrics (RMSE, DTW and coverage) for the performance (expected delay, peak-to-average ratio and worst-case load). We conducted our experiments and showed that GenAI-based decision pipelines significantly outperform traditional baselines for predictive accuracy as well as case diversity and decision robustness in real world smart city data. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: This paper examines the problem of modeling and planning the movement of an autonomous mobile robot in a university technology park characterized by high uncertainty, a multi-zone structure, and intensive interaction with personnel. It is shown that classical route planning algorithms do not provide the required adaptability and safety in an environment with variable human density and dynamic production priorities. A two-level algorithm for planning the motion of an industrial mobile robot is proposed, including fuzzy decision-making and classical navigation. The fuzzy model considers task urgency, distance to the target, population density, technology park zone type, and safety restrictions, generating an integrated route assessment and recommended speed. The technology park structure, robot status, and fuzzy rule base are formalized, enabling adaptive route selection in real time. Simulation experiment on 100 routes was conducted, comparing the proposed approach with the A* and Dijkstra algorithms. The simulation results showed that the fuzzy algorithm reduces the integrated risk indicator by an average of 40–45% and the number of route replanning. This confirms the feasibility of using fuzzy-logic and hybrid planning methods for mobile robots operating in the multifunctional environments of university technology parks. The results obtained can be used in the design of intelligent logistics systems integrated with MES/ERP and digital twins of production complexes. © European Alliance for Innovation 2027.

Abstract: The recent developments in data-driven methods have paved the way for new methodologies to provide accurate and robust full state reconstruction of engineering systems under any operating conditions. Such approaches can be attractive for next-generation nuclear reactors, which represent particularly challenging applications for sensing and monitoring due to the complexity of the strongly coupled physics involved and the extremely harsh environments. Data-driven techniques can combine different sources of information, including computational proxy models and noisy measurements on the system, to robustly estimate the state. This work leverages the novel Shallow Recurrent Decoder (SHRED) architecture to infer the entire state vector (both neutronics and fluid dynamics fields) of a circulating fuel reactor, the Molten Salt Fast Reactor. The standard architecture is extended to treat parametric time-series data, ensuring the possibility of investigating different scenarios and showing its capabilities to provide an accurate state estimation in various conditions. The proposed methodology adopts possible innovative sensing strategies in new-generation reactors, including out-of-core time-series neutron flux measurements alone, in-core sensing measuring the precursor concentrations or mobile probes advected by the fuel flow. The promising results of this work are further strengthened by the possibility of quantifying the uncertainty associated with the state estimation due to the considerably low training cost of the architecture. The ability of SHRED to deliver real-time, system-wide reconstruction highlights its potential for reactor monitoring, control, and digital twin development in next-generation circulating fuel systems. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Flotation Kinetics Beyond the First-Order Paradigm: A Multi-Scale, Heterogeneity-Aware Framework for Coal and Complex Minerals
Affiliations: Department of Mining Engineering, Higher Education Complex of Zarand, Shahid Bahonar University of Kerman, Zarand, 77611-46934, Iran; ElementUSA, Cedar Park, 78613, TX, United States

Abstract: For nearly a century, flotation kinetics has relied on deterministic first-order rate equations treating the cell as a homogeneous reactor, a paradigm that faces significant limitations for heterogeneous ores, especially coal, whose organic macerals, porosity, and oxidation susceptibility defy a single rate constant. While more advanced distributed-k, mixed-order, and population-balance models can account for certain types of particle heterogeneity (e.g., size or liberation), they still assume that the floatability distribution remains invariant during flotation, an assumption that fails when surface chemistry evolves concurrently with the separation process. Breaking from chronological cataloguing, this review proposes a three-dimensional taxonomy based on physical scale, inherent material heterogeneity, and epistemic certainty. We demonstrate that critical industrial prediction failures arise from structural mismatches between model physics and particle surface chemistry, notably time-dependent oxidation deactivation and selective maceral recovery. Six fundamental failure modes are identified, from neglected time-dependence of rate constants to the absence of a thermodynamic deactivation term, corroborated by experimental evidence from coal and base-metal flotation. Advanced microfluidic, automated mineralogical, surface-sensitive spectromicroscopic, CFD-DEM, and physics-informed machine learning tools are dismantling the black box of the flotation rate constant “k”. We introduce the Distributed Reactive Surface Kinetics (DRSK) framework, which embeds particle-scale heterogeneity into a population balance via an adaptive surface-sensitive selection function and treats kinetic uncertainty through stochastic differential equations. A comprehensive comparison table facilitates the transition from conventional models to the DRSK paradigm. We conclude with a roadmap for flotation kinetics 4.0, where digital twins, real-time froth analytics, and self-calibrating hybrid models transform this empirical discipline into a truly predictive engineering science. Quantitative validation against published coal and copper flotation data demonstrates that DRSK reduces prediction error by 60%–75% compared to conventional first-order and distributed-k models, while providing probabilistic uncertainty bounds essential for risk-based decision-making. The framework is elaborated for coal and conventional minerals, underscoring why coal demands its own dedicated kinetic theory and how these lessons can revolutionize the processing of increasingly complex, low-grade ores and secondary resources. © 2026 by the authors.

Abstract: The rapid development of Electric Vehicle (EV) has increased the demand for battery management systems (BMSs) capable of ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient operation under dynamic conditions. This review critically examines the evolution of EV-BMS technologies from conventional monitoring and protection to AI-enabled, connected, and application-oriented systems. Unlike reviews that primarily address individual BMS functions or specific battery technologies, this work integrates battery characteristics and degradation with state estimation, thermal management, cell balancing, fault diagnosis, safety, and emerging BMS architectures, while emphasizing their interactions and practical deployment constraints. Recent developments in machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, physics-informed methods, cloud-assisted and digital-twin-based BMS, wireless communication, cybersecurity, and emerging battery chemistries are comparatively examined in terms of computational burden, data requirements, safety, scalability, and real-time applicability. The review further identifies system-level challenges related to cross-chemistry transferability, uncertainty and sensor faults, AI validation, communication reliability, cloud-edge coordination, and BMS adaptation for emerging and second-life batteries. These findings highlight the need to move beyond isolated algorithmic improvements toward validated, interoperable, and application-aware BMS architectures for future EVs. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: AI4Land: A Scalable Deep Learning Framework on MareNostrum5 for Global High-Resolution Land Use Reconstruction

Abstract: Uncertainty in the terrestrial carbon cycle remains a major constraint in climate projections, partly driven by the uncertainties affecting the land surface representation and variability in Earth system models. To address this limitation, we present a data-driven framework - AI4Land - for generating high-resolution historical reconstructions and future projections of key land surface variables. The framework follows a two-phase approach using a U-Net architecture. In the first phase, which is the focus of this work, it reconstructs annual land use and land cover by integrating coarse-resolution scenario data with static geophysical features. In a planned second phase, the resulting high-resolution maps will be used to predict dynamic biophysical variables, particularly leaf area index, at finer temporal scales. Trained on Earth observation data, the models learn to reproduce spatially explicit and physically consistent land surface patterns, extending temporal coverage to periods lacking direct observations. AI4Land was developed and trained on MareNostrum5, demonstrating how GPU-accelerated HPC infrastructure enables global-scale climate AI pipelines. The final product is a suite of open-source emulators designed for real-time coupling with digital twin platforms, such as those developed under the Destination Earth initiative. By delivering realistic and evolving land surface conditions on demand, this work aims to reduce critical uncertainties and improve the predictive power of next-generation climate simulations. 2026 The Authors. Abstract: The efficient separation and recovery of lithium from spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBR) remains a critical challenge in hydrometallurgical recycling, primarily due to its significant and dispersed losses throughout the multistage purification process. This study addresses this bottleneck by developing a high-fidelity, steady-state mathematic model for an entire LIBR process. The model, which has been rigorously validated against plant data, serves as a digital twin to quantitatively diagnose the loss path of lithium. A full-process elemental flow analysis revealed that lithium recovery was the key limiting factor, with a process yield of only 61.08%, compared to >92% for nickel and cobalt. The analysis pinpointed the leaching and final precipitation units as primary loss sources, identifying soluble Li+ (81.94%) and insoluble LiF (17.94%) as the dominant loss forms. A systematic sensitivity analysis was then conducted to deconvolute the effects of key separation parameters: a reasonable pH of the leaching process is recommended to be 2.0 at the process temperature, and the operating pressure of the lithium precipitation unit should be higher than 1.6 bar to reduce entrainment losses. Implementing these optimized conditions led to an increase in the lithium carbonate precipitation ratio, thereby raising the final lithium recovery to 70.47%. A coupled techno-economic analysis confirmed the viability of the optimization strategy. Although the unit production cost increased by 2.3%, the enhanced lithium yield increased the unit net profit by 3.8%, which also shifted the revenue structure, making Li2CO3 the dominant product. Furthermore, the uncertainty analysis further reveals that the profitability of the LIBR process is most sensitive to the cost of raw materials and the prices of lithium and cobalt products. This work demonstrates a closed-loop methodology that integrates process simulation, bottleneck diagnosis, targeted optimization, and techno-economic verification to systematically improve the separation efficiency and economic potential of complex resource recovery processes. © 2026 American Chemical Society

Abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly recognised as a promising solution for food supply chains (FSCs). However, existing DT research has focused mainly on conceptual development, technical applications, and pilot implementations, providing limited empirical evidence on the determinants influencing firms’ adoption decisions. Thus, this study examines the determinants of DT adoption decisions in FSCs. Drawing on Diffusion of Innovation theory and the technology–organisation–environment (TOE) framework, the study develops a research model explaining how TOE factors shape firms’ adoption decisions. Survey data from 260 respondents in food and technology-related firms across Western economies are analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Results show that compatibility, technology readiness, top management support, competitive pressure, and market uncertainty significantly influence the DT adoption decision, while complexity negatively affects adoption. Findings indicate that the DT adoption decision in FSCs is shaped not only by perceived technological characteristics but also by organisational support and external environmental pressures. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Digital Twin-oriented optimizer selection for volatility-sensitive manufacturing scheduling
Affiliations: Department of Business Administration, University of Patras, Patras, 26504, Greece
Authors with affiliations: Nearchou A.C., Department of Business Administration, University of Patras, Patras, 26504, Greece
Abstract: The increasing adoption of Digital Twin (DT) technologies in smart manufacturing has created the need for adaptive scheduling intelligence capable of operating under volatile and uncertain energy environments. Existing studies typically assume that a single optimization algorithm can effectively operate across all manufacturing conditions. However, optimization effectiveness is strongly influenced by energy volatility, uncertainty and production-context characteristics. This paper proposes a DT-oriented hyper-heuristic framework for adaptive optimizer selection in manufacturing scheduling. An offline Pareto optimization knowledge repository is constructed using nine representative multi-objective optimization (MOO) paradigms evaluated under multiple industrial energy scenarios with different volatility regimes. The resulting optimization knowledge is subsequently exploited to train a hyper-heuristic selector capable of recommending suitable optimization paradigms according to the prevailing DT operating conditions. To evaluate cross-environment robustness, a leave-one-scenario-out (LOSO) validation strategy is adopted using previously unseen energy conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that optimizer effectiveness is highly context-dependent and that the proposed framework consistently identifies near-optimal optimization paradigms associated with relatively low regret. Explainable decision-landscape analysis further reveals structured optimizer-selection transitions across different volatility regions, highlighting the strong interaction between energy-market dynamics and adaptive optimization behavior. © 2026 The Author

Title: Advancing Renewable Energy Integration Through Energy Storage Systems: A Policy, Economic, Social, and Technological Perspective
Affiliations: Centre for Excellence - Research, Rajalakshmi Engineering College, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India
Authors with affiliations: Jayabal R., Centre for Excellence - Research, Rajalakshmi Engineering College, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India
Abstract: The growing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) has increased demand for flexible, reliable energy storage systems (ESS) to compensate for intermittency and ensure grid stability. This review critically assesses the most common ESS types from technical and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled perspectives, as well as political, economic, sociocultural, and technological (PEST) aspects. Lithium-ion batteries suit short and medium duration applications, offering high round trip efficiency, energy density, and fast response. In contrast, flow batteries, pumped hydroelectric storage (PHE), compressed-air energy storage, hydrogen, and thermal storage are better suited to long-duration and bulk energy applications. The review also investigates data-driven forecasting, energy management, state-of-charge and state-of-health estimation, predictive maintenance, digital twins, and AI-assisted grid operation. The comparative evaluation shows that no single storage technology meets the requirements for efficiency, duration, scalability, cost, safety, and lifecycle sustainability. Therefore, hybrid storage schemes can capture the best of multiple features across different operating timescales. Significant deployment challenges include capital cost, degradation, recycling, data availability, cybersecurity, regulatory uncertainty, and inadequate standardization. New avenues being explored include second-life batteries, long-duration storage, explainable and federated AI, digital twins, virtual power plants (VPPs), and circular material strategies. Harmonious breakthroughs in storage technology, smart/optimal control, policy, economic, and life cycle sustainability without compromising resilience, flexibility, and renewable penetration are urgently needed to enable clean power systems. © 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

Title: Machine learning for rarefied gas transport in vacuum and micro/nano systems: Demonstrated capabilities, deployment requirements, and a research roadmap
Affiliations: Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, University of Massachusetts Amherst, Amherst, 01003, MA, United States
Authors with affiliations: Roohi E., Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, University of Massachusetts Amherst, Amherst, 01003, MA, United States
Abstract: Machine learning (ML) now serves several distinct roles in rarefied-gas modeling. Learned components can be embedded in kinetic solvers, and surrogate models can distribute the cost of an expensive calculation over repeated queries. Fast forward models can support parameter inference from measurements. Published studies report complete-solver acceleration of a kinetic Fokker–Planck method, a reduction in the runtime of ab initio direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC), percent-level errors at withheld flow conditions, and improved accuracy near shocks through physics-based representations. These results establish useful capabilities within stated test ranges, although they do not support unrestricted extrapolation. This Perspective classifies these uses according to the reference solver, training data, physical constraints, deployment range, and online task. The classification covers deterministic kinetic methods, DSMC, particle Fokker–Planck solvers, moment methods, molecular and ab initio models, and free-molecular test-particle simulation. The article distinguishes kernel, complete-solver, and lifecycle costs and describes implementation paths for conductance design, Knudsen-pump optimization, gas–surface inference, and vacuum-system digital twins. It also proposes a benchmark manifest based on microchannel mass flow, Knudsen pumps, vacuum conductance, and 70-degree blunted-cone experiments. Reliable deployment requires physical constraints, evaluation that accounts for sampling noise, propagation of accommodation uncertainty, and comparison with experiments. Kinetic solvers therefore remain the source of physical structure and certification even when ML changes how often and where those solvers are used. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A physics-oriented review of neural-network-based modeling for bluff-body flows

Abstract: Bluff-body flows combine early separation, coherent wake organization, vortex shedding, and strong sensitivity to geometry, Reynolds number, inflow condition, and three-dimensional transition. These features make them both canonical fluid-mechanics benchmarks and demanding targets for neural-network-based modeling. This review provides a representative, physics-oriented synthesis of neural-network approaches for bluff-body flows. Instead of organizing the field by architecture or prediction task, the review asks which wake mechanisms current models represent and which validation evidence makes those claims trustworthy. It examines how current models represent separation, wake topology, pressure-wake coupling, coherent shedding, turbulence statistics, closure behavior, and flow-control mechanisms. We discuss data sources, flow representations, model classes, validation practices, and practical uses in surrogate prediction, reconstruction, monitoring, control, and digital-twin-type workflows. The review emphasizes that low numerical error by itself does not establish physical learning, and argues for validation based on topology, spectra, force response, uncertainty, generalization, and interpretable mechanism evidence. © 2026 Author(s).

Abstract: Precision livestock farming requires accurate and timely heat stress prediction to ensure animal welfare and optimize farm management. This study presents a physics-informed digital twin (DT) framework combined with an uncertainty-aware, expert-weighted stacked ensemble for multimodal forecasting of Core Body Temperature (CBT) in dairy cattle. Using the high-frequency, heterogeneous MmCows dataset, the DT integrates an ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based thermoregulation model that simulates metabolic heat production and dissipation, a Gaussian process for capturing cow-specific deviations, a Kalman filter for aligning predictions with real-time sensor data, and a behavioral Markov chain that models activity-state transitions under varying environmental conditions. The DT outputs key physiological indicators, such as predicted CBT, heat stress probability, and behavioral state distributions are fused with raw sensor data and enriched through multi-scale temporal analysis and cross-modal feature engineering to form a comprehensive feature set. The predictive methodology is designed in a three-stage stacked ensemble, where stage 1 trains modality-specific LightGBM ‘expert’ models on distinct feature groups, stage 2 collects their predictions as meta-features, and at stage 3 Optuna-tuned LightGBM meta-model yields the final CBT forecast. Predictive uncertainty is quantified via bootstrapping and validated using Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP). Ablation analysis confirms that incorporating DT-derived features and multimodal fusion substantially enhances performance. The proposed framework achieves a cross-validated R2 of 0.783, F1 score of 84.25% and PICP of 92.38% for 2-hour ahead forecasting, providing a robust, uncertainty-aware, and physically principled system for early heat stress detection and precision livestock management. © 2026

Abstract: The reliable long-term prediction of photovoltaic (PV) system performance is essential for optimizing operation, maintenance, and energy management in smart cities. Digital Twin (DT) technology has emerged as a promising approach for real-time monitoring and predictive analytics by continuously integrating physical system measurements with virtual models. However, many existing DT-based studies rely on limited validation periods, lack comprehensive uncertainty quantification, and provide insufficient comparisons with conventional forecasting approaches. To address these limitations, this study proposes a data-driven Digital Twin framework for daily photovoltaic energy production prediction for three silicon photovoltaic technologies (amorphous silicon, polycrystalline silicon, and monocrystalline silicon) operating under semi-arid climatic conditions in Morocco. The framework integrates data quality assessment and statistical production trend analysis based on linear regression, bootstrap confidence intervals, the Mann–Kendall trend test, and Sen’s slope estimator. In addition, the proposed DT model was benchmarked against persistence, linear regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models using a chronological training, validation, and independent testing framework. Model performance was evaluated over an independent test period of 602 consecutive days, representing approximately 1.65 years of continuous operation and more than one complete annual cycle. The proposed Digital Twin improved upon the standalone LightGBM model, achieving an RMSE of 1.3047 kWh/day, an MAE of 0.9255 kWh/day, a MAPE of 14.62%, and an R2 of 0.7015, compared with an RMSE of 1.3349 kWh/day, an MAE of 0.9637 kWh/day, and an R2 of 0.6875 for LightGBM. Over the 11-year monitoring period, the estimated long-term production trend rates were −0.566% yr−1 for a-Si, −0.335% yr−1 for pc-Si, and −0.260% yr−1 for mc-Si. Bootstrap analysis yielded median long-term production trend rates of −0.573, −0.326, and −0.251% yr−1, respectively, while Mann–Kendall tests indicated no statistically significant monotonic production trend for any technology (p = 0.1611, 0.2758, and 0.3502, respectively). The extended independent testing period, combined with statistical production trend analysis and comparative machine-learning evaluation, demonstrates the applicability of the proposed Digital Twin framework for photovoltaic performance monitoring and adaptive prediction under semi-arid climatic conditions. © 2026 by the authors.

Author full names: Anafina, Aida (60980182400); Kornilova, Alla (60980316500)
Title: Digital and bioinspired approaches to designing sustainable educational spaces: Modeling, optimization, and adaptive systems
Affiliations: Department, S. Seifullin Kazakh Agrotechnical Research University, Kazakhstan
Authors with affiliations: Anafina A., Department, S. Seifullin Kazakh Agrotechnical Research University, Kazakhstan; Kornilova A., Department, S. Seifullin Kazakh Agrotechnical Research University, Kazakhstan
Abstract: This study presents a mathematically rigorous, digitally bio-inspired framework for sustainable educational space design. Integrating parametric Building Information Modeling (BIM), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), surrogate response modeling, bio-inspired multi-objective optimization, and interval type-2 fuzzy adaptive control, the methodology is applied to a prototypical 4,860 m² learning center governed by fifteen decision variables. The optimization formulation simultaneously minimizes energy use intensity, discomfort hours, operational carbon, acoustic penalty, and daylight deficiency while maximizing graph-based spatial flexibility. Evaluating genetic algorithms, self-adaptive particle swarm optimization (SAPSO), and ant colony optimization across hypervolume and composite sustainability indices, SAPSO proved optimal. It reduced energy use intensity from 154.2 to 93.7 kWh/m²·yr, operational carbon from 127.8 to 75.4 kgCO₂e/m²·yr, thermal discomfort from 418 to 143 h/yr, and reverberation time from 0.92 to 0.59 s, while boosting useful daylight illuminance from 54% to 81%. Additionally, interval type-2 fuzzy control yielded a further 17.6% in daily energy savings over rule-based operations. Architecturally interpreted through spatial typology, circulation, acoustic privacy, and user experience, the mathematical engine directly informs spatial design without supplanting human architectural judgment. © The Author 2026.

Title: Quantum-Inspired Graph Neural Digital Twins for the sub-microsecond topological co-design and temporal degradation modeling of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin smart gels
Affiliations: Bajpai & Co. Research Private Limited (Bajpai Labs), Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow, India
Authors with affiliations: Bajpai K., Bajpai & Co. Research Private Limited (Bajpai Labs), Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow, India
Abstract: The clinical translation of lignocellulosic smart gels is constrained by empirical formulation screening, complex structure–property relationships, and uncertainty in degradation and therapeutic-release behavior. This study aims to determine whether a unified computational digital-twin framework can (i) optimize the crosslinking topology of cellulose-, hemicellulose-, and lignin-based matrices, (ii) predict their mechanical and temporal degradation behavior, and (iii) translate optimized formulations into real-time control parameters for microfluidic synthesis. To address these objectives, we develop a Quantum-Inspired Graph Neural Digital Twin (Q-GNDT) that represents molecular interactions as dynamic non-Euclidean graphs and formulates topological optimization as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. A temporal graph-decay model couples pH-dependent hydrolysis, enzymatic cleavage, percolation loss, and drug diffusion to predict time-resolved degradation and release. The computational architecture is integrated with an edge-AI control model designed for sub-microsecond microfluidic actuation. Retrospective cross-validation against published experimental datasets from three independent studies yielded mean absolute errors of 2.1% for pore size, 2.9% for storage modulus, and 1.5% for drug-release kinetics, with an overall RMSE of 0.74%. An in-silico targeted-delivery case study further produced 4.1% initial burst release, 98.0% cumulative delivery, and near-linear release kinetics (R2 = 0.991). These results indicate that Q-GNDT can serve as a computational design and screening framework for narrowing the experimental search space of programmable lignocellulosic biomaterials. Prospective synthesis, biological testing, and in vivo validation remain necessary before clinical translation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Abstract: Introduction: Multi-Energy Virtual Power Plants (MEVPPs) integrating Waste-to-Energy Plants (WEPs), distributed renewables, and Electric Vehicles (EVs) offer low-carbon benefits, yet their uncertainties—fluctuating WEP output, stochastic wind/solar generation, and erratic EV charging—hinder accurate quantification of environmental performance. This study aims to precisely characterize these uncertainties and enhance MEVPP coordination via a combined physical-data modeling approach. Methods: A Distributed Model Predictive Control (DMPC) method based on digital twins is proposed. Specifically, a five-stage physical-digital hybrid digital twin model captures WEP uncertainty; dynamic adaptive spectral clustering and weighted capacity aggregation address spatial heterogeneity of distributed wind/solar; a truncated-gamma-distribution-based ordered charging model handles EV uncertainty. A multi-timescale DMPC framework (day-ahead planning, intraday rolling, real-time adjustment) is established. Results: The hybrid digital twin improved WEP output prediction accuracy by 41% over single-data models, and renewable prediction under sudden weather events by 42.3%. Compared with stochastic MPC, robust MPC, and a consensus-ADMM DMPC baseline, our scheme reduced operating cost by 5.2%-7.1% and computation time by 36.3%-82.5%, while maintaining constraint-violation rate below 0.21%. Discussion: These findings underscore that the hybrid physical-digital framework effectively mitigates multiple uncertainties, enabling more reliable scheduling and significant computational savings. The robustness is further validated across summer, winter, high-renewable, and stressed weather scenarios, alongside sensitivity analyses on EV penetration, wind-to-solar ratio, and carbon pricing, confirming broad applicability under diverse operational conditions. Conclusion: The proposed DMPC with digital-twin enhancement substantially improves scheduling accuracy, operational efficiency, and low-carbon performance of MEVPP, providing a practical pathway for promoting renewable integration and supporting the "dual carbon" goals. 2026, The Author(s). Abstract: Preferential seepage becomes evidence of internal erosion only when the hydraulic response can be linked to particle detachment and transport. This critical review examines that distinction in embankment dams and levees, considering how transient loading, storage, and geological structure affect both the physical process and its observation. Hydraulic records establish the response to changing loads, while thermal and geophysical surveys help constrain possible pathways. Particle sampling and investigation of sediment sources provide evidence of material loss that these indirect observations cannot establish alone. Joint interpretation of lag, attenuation, hysteresis, recession, and spatial coherence helps distinguish regional groundwater and bank-storage responses from localized seepage. The comparison of sensing and inverse methods shows why resolution, uncertainty, and verification must be assessed for the particular question being asked. We propose an evidence hierarchy and an observation-conditioned event tree to connect these interpretations with engineering decisions. For learned models and digital twins, testing on unseen events and assets, independent physical checks, and the consequences of false and missed alarms are central to evaluating practical benefit. The review emphasizes physically grounded, site-specific interpretation and verification as the basis for diagnosis and warning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Large language models, ChatGPT, and beyond: A new paradigm for condition monitoring and prognosis in power and energy systems
Affiliations: University of Brest, UMR CNRS 6027 IRDL, Brest, France
Authors with affiliations: Benbouzid M., University of Brest, UMR CNRS 6027 IRDL, Brest, France
Abstract: Large language models and related foundation models offer new capabilities for interpreting heterogeneous information, retrieving engineering knowledge, and supporting high-level decision processes in power and energy systems. This Perspective examines their role in condition monitoring and prognostics and health management, with particular emphasis on remaining useful life estimation. To support language and multimodal model interpretation of structured and validated estimates, we propose a digital twin-centric architecture comprising physics-guided hybrid estimation, digital twin synchronization, rule-governed semantic translation, foundation model reasoning, output validation, and human supervision. The specific contribution is threefold. First, the proposed layering principle distinguishes physically consistent estimation, system integration, and higher-level reasoning functions. Second, an auditable semantic interface is defined to encode health indicators, degradation states, remaining useful life distributions, uncertainty information, operating context, provenance, retrieved evidence, and permitted reasoning scope. Third, a deployment-oriented reliability framework relates physical consistency, digital twin consistency, explanation fidelity, uncertainty preservation, robustness, traceability, safe deferral, latency, data sensitivity, and computational requirements to edge, on premises, cloud, and hybrid implementations. An illustrative battery state-of-health and remaining useful life use case demonstrates the resulting information flow. The foundation model layer is primarily intended for slow-timescale, human-supervised functions such as diagnostic explanation, degradation interpretation, maintenance prioritization, inspection planning, and fleet-level assessment, rather than protection or real-time control. The Perspective also examines complementary roles for small language models, tiny recursive models, world models, large language models, and multimodal foundation models and identifies priorities for their reliable evaluation and deployment in power and energy prognostics and health management. © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: Manufacturing processes and production systems are becoming increasingly sophisticated, while market demand and external conditions are rapidly evolving. In this context, the adoption of digital twin technology has been expanding to maintain manufacturing competitiveness by enabling the prediction of system performance under various uncertainties and the optimization of operational decisions. The accuracy of prediction and analysis based on digital twins largely depends on the fidelity of the digital model, which represents how precisely the real manufacturing system is replicated. In general, high-fidelity models can provide results that closely approximate real-world system behavior. However, such models incur significant simulation time and cost due to increased model complexity and data requirements. As a result, directly applying high-fidelity digital twins to real-world production decision-making remains challenging. This study defines the concept of digital twin fidelity for production operations and proposes a workflow for its systematic design. In particular, digital twin fidelity for production optimization is structured into four dimensions–Geometry, Attribute, Data Synchronization, and Operational Logic–each specified in terms of detailed elements and corresponding levels. The proposed workflow supports the selection of appropriate fidelity levels according to different optimization objectives and operational scenarios. A case study is conducted to validate the proposed workflow by developing a workflow-based low-fidelity digital twin model and applying it to a production optimization problem. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces simulation time compared to a high-fidelity digital twin model, while achieving identical optimization outcomes. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Abstract: Additive manufacturing is relying more and more on artificial intelligence for prediction, control, and real-time decisions. Deployment, however, is still difficult. The main reason is that the underlying thermal, flow, and microstructural behavior can shift as the process changes, which makes reliable model performance hard to maintain. This review examines how trustworthy artificial intelligence (TAI) can be used to close that gap in digital twins for additive manufacturing across both metallic and ceramic systems. It frames trustworthiness as a technical condition for deployment and translates it into an AM-specific operational framework. From that point onward, it examines how current workflows handle reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, explainability, robustness, generalizability, fairness, and transparency. A structured evaluation of sixty studies in metallic and ceramic additive manufacturing systems reveals a distinct trend. Robustness and generalizability receive much more attention than transparency, explainability, and fairness. The coverage is also stronger in metallic systems than in ceramic ones. To move beyond binary classification, the review further applies a structured evidence-depth rubric that distinguishes absent coverage, limited or implicit evidence, method-level evidence, and operational evidence for each TAI attribute. We further show that trustworthy deployment depends on more than predictive accuracy. It also depends on physically consistent models as well as updates that account for uncertainty. Decision support has to remain interpretable as well. Model transfer across machines and materials should be treated as controlled adaptation, where reusable physics, sensing, and validation elements are separated from material-specific features that require recalibration. The validation path must also support qualification and industrial deployment, leading to a more cohesive digital twin framework. It brings together physics-based models, reduced-order models, learning-based surrogates, multimodal sensing, and trust-aware evaluation. The main finding is that trustworthiness is the missing technical link between digital twins that can be confidently used in advanced manufacturing and promising AI-enabled demonstrations. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Physics-informed digital twin for optimal operation of solar air source heat pump-based district heating systems
